1 · Intro

When to use it.

A paid intern is an employee. They are hired, paid, and set up like any other worker of their type.

An unpaid internship is allowed under federal wage law only when the intern, not the employer, is the primary beneficiary of the arrangement. The Department of Labor's Fact Sheet #71 explains the test courts use.

Use this whenSomeone wants to bring on an intern, and you need to know whether the person must be paid and how to set them up.

Watch-outs

  • An unpaid intern who does regular work for the department may legally be an employee. Decide before the start date, not after.
  • Open item: confirm with your engagement consultant (EC) which Oracle worker type and category Vanderbilt uses for paid and unpaid interns, and which checks apply.
  • Open item: confirm with your EC whether any state where the intern works has stricter internship rules.

HCM Academy job aid · Hiring

Interns (Paid and Unpaid)

Use when: Someone wants to bring on an intern, and you need to know whether the person must be paid and how to set them up. · System: Overview

  1. Start with one question: will the intern be paid?
  2. For an unpaid internship, apply the primary beneficiary test.
    • Clear understanding that there is no pay.
    • Training similar to an educational setting.
    • Tied to coursework or academic credit, and to the academic calendar.
  3. Check that the intern does not displace paid work.
  4. Limit the internship to its learning period.
  5. If the test is unclear, treat it as paid and ask.
  6. Set up the person with the right worker type and checks.
